build 3: Flow set by evaporative demand (light, wind, humidity, stomatal opening), with the dye front advected at that rate, is honest but simple, essentially a demand formula plus advection. The leaf-pore zoom and the tree-scale bucket count are illustrations rather than model output.

runnersUp.title: TLS: how a connection becomes private
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A real protocol mechanism (key share, certificate chain, forward secrecy) with a strong MITM toggle, honestly level 3 and distinct from cryptography's separate primitives, though its prerequisite elliptic-curve-cryptography is only a pool candidate.

build 3: Buildable with real X25519/ECDSA and HKDF through WebCrypto or a small library and a real public certificate chain, so the MITM failure and forward secrecy are computed, not drawn. It needs care, because a stepped protocol page drifts easily into a browse-a-diagram of message boxes.

runnersUp.title: Galois theory: why the quintic has no formula
judgeNotes: build 3: Tracking the roots numerically while the coefficients move and recording the permutation is buildable and honest, but Arnold's nested-commutator argument for degree 5 needs carefully precomputed loops, and the commutator depth is an argument the page shows rather than a model it computes, so this is a hard page to make legible.

fit-level 4: Arnold's topological proof, with roots permuting as coefficients loop, is a rare case where a deep theorem gets a genuine animated mechanism. It is a distinctive level-3 draw, though hard to build well.

runnersUp.title: How a web page is drawn
judgeNotes: build 3: Buildable only with a deliberately tiny HTML subset parser, selector matcher and block/inline layout engine; the scope is large and risks a stepped diagram, so it must restrict itself to a stated subset of CSS.
fit-level 4: Parsing, style matching, layout and paint form a real pipeline that a level-1 reader can follow on editable HTML, and the page picks up where the internet page stops.

runnersUp.title: Heat transfer: conduction, convection & radiation
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A much-wanted, honest level-1 mechanism page (heat through a wall, convection cells, radiation) that no existing page shows, since entropy only equalises particle temperatures; trim it to the wall and keep the pan and radiator as short steps so it stays one graphic.

build 3: The conduction core is an honest, small 1D/2D heat equation on a grid through a wall with a tabulated k (facts, no licence issue). The pan-convection, radiator and thermal-camera add-ons are not modelled, though: honest convection needs a fluid solver, and the others are pictures. Narrow it to the wall/insulation model with a U-value meter.

runnersUp.title: How a broken bone mends
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A clear staged mechanism (haematoma, soft callus, hard callus, remodelling) with one honest control (cast vs movement) that a 10-year-old who has seen a cast will follow; distinct from bridges-structures and from the level-3 bone-remodelling candidate.

build 3: A grid where callus ossifies where strain is low and is resorbed where unloaded is a real (if crude) mechanobiology rule and runs easily, but the hematoma-callus-remodel stages risk being a scripted timeline rather than an outcome of the rule; the build must make the non-union and thin-bone results emerge from the grid.

runnersUp.title: Mantle convection
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A Rayleigh-number convection box with a stagnant lid and Nusselt scaling is the real model behind plate-tectonics and is clearly university geophysics.

build 3: Isoviscous infinite-Prandtl convection (a streamfunction biharmonic solved by FFT or multigrid on about 128x64) is interactive, but the stagnant-lid and plate-like regimes need viscosity contrasts of 10^4 or more and fine grids at high Rayleigh number, so the solve is stiff and slow; limit the contrast range and precompute the Nusselt-Rayleigh plot, or the lid-foundering part will not run live.

runnersUp.title: Tap to pay
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A battery-less card powered by the reader's pulsing magnetism is an everyday mystery with a clear mechanism of power against distance, kept simpler than and distinct from electromagnetism.

build 3: Coupling between coaxial loops against distance with a wake-up threshold is honest but thin: mostly one meter against distance. 'Stack two cards and the reader cannot tell them apart' is wrong, because ISO 14443 anticollision tells cards apart and payment terminals detect the clash and refuse; it also cites a metal-detector page that is not in this batch.

runnersUp.title: What a fire needs
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Fuel-heat-air with one control removed at a time is a standard primary-school topic with a clear mechanism, distinct from the level-2 reaction-rates page; absorb the jar-weight idea from candle-under-a-jar.
build 3: The oxygen-depletion part is a real small model, but the water, wet-cloth and wick-cutting controls are rule toggles. It is nearly the same page as candle-under-a-jar, so merge them.

runnersUp.title: Cooking an egg
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Proteins unfolding and tangling irreversibly with heat is a clear mechanism from a universal experience, distinct from level-2 protein-folding, with a single thermometer control.

build 3: Threshold denaturation temperatures are published facts, so it is buildable. But the honest model needs heat conduction into the egg over time (time-at-temperature, first-order kinetics), not a dragged thermometer. The grey ring (iron sulfide) is not modelled.

runnersUp.title: Electrolysis
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Electrolysis is core secondary-school chemistry with a clear particle mechanism; it is the reverse of redox-batteries and adds the discharge rules and the charge-to-mass relation.

build 3: Ion drift and charge counting (Faraday) are a real, small particle model, but which ion is discharged in solution comes from a lookup rule in the reactivity series rather than from the model, and the aluminium-cell coda is a picture; data are only reference constants.

runnersUp.title: Superconductivity
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Zero resistance, field expulsion and the BCS gap form a real level-3 model and a popular subject; it is ambitious in scope and depends on bose-einstein-condensation from the pool.

build 3: The London-equation grid, the numerical BCS gap equation and an RCSJ junction ODE are each buildable, but zero resistance would just be set rather than modelled, and four loosely joined models risk becoming a slideshow; it needs narrowing to one or two mechanisms.

runnersUp.title: Why some volcanoes explode and others ooze
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Viscosity trapping gas, shown as fizz versus burst, is the mechanism plate-tectonics never shows and works with one control for a 10-year-old.

build 3: Decompression bubble growth, Stokes rise of bubbles through a magma of chosen viscosity, and fragmentation above about 75 percent gas fraction can be computed in a 1D conduit, but the model is coarse and risks becoming a two-ending story unless the eruption style follows from the computed gas fraction.

runnersUp.title: Why onions make you cry
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A familiar experience explained by one clear mechanism (cutting a cell mixes two separated ingredients), with honest single-variable remedies, at level 0, and distinct from the-cell.

build 3: Buildable as a cell grid (each cut cell releases gas) feeding a 2D advection-diffusion field, but the four controls are just scale factors on one release term, so it leans toward an animated cartoon; the garlic comparison is a different reaction and should be a separate parameter set, not a cosmetic swap.

runnersUp.title: Why leaves change colour
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A universally seen phenomenon with a crisp mechanism (green dismantled, yellow unmasked, red made fresh) that one weather control drives, and the reverse of the photosynthesis page.

build 3: Three pigment pools driven by day length, temperature and light, with leaf colour mixed from the pigment fractions, can be built and gives an honest qualitative model for level 0, but the rate constants have no source and the result is close to a scripted colour ramp; mixing from measured absorption spectra (licence to check) would make it more than a picture.

runnersUp.title: The nitrogen cycle
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Bacteria as gatekeepers and eutrophication form a real agent mechanism that is widely taught at high-school level, and distinct from carbon-cycle and ecosystems.

build 3: The bacterial agent model is buildable but its rates are invented, which makes it a dressed-up diagram, and adding eutrophication puts a second model on the page; the Fowler et al. 2013 licence is unconfirmed, so build a stoichiometric box model with literature rates and a qualitative diagram, or scale it down.

runnersUp.title: Mass, binding energy & the valley of stability
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: The binding-energy curve and the valley of stability explain why both fission and fusion release energy, which neither existing nuclear page shows; the level 2 is honest, but level-2 slots are scarce in this round.

build 3: The AME2020/NUBASE2020 values are freely downloadable facts and the papers are CC BY 3.0, but the files carry no licence and only ask for citation, which leaves the data partly unconfirmed. As described, the page is mostly a chart to browse; adding a semi-empirical mass formula the reader can fit against the data would make it a real model.

runnersUp.title: Electricity at home
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A well-placed level-1 bridge between electric-circuits and power-grid with visible mechanisms (AC on a scope, fuse, earth fault, breaker); its transformer step repeats power-grid's, so keep that part brief.

build 3: The sine-wave oscilloscope, P=VI current draw, kWh meter, fuse threshold and transformer turns ratio are all trivially computable. But the earth-fault and breaker scenes are rule-driven animations rather than a model, so the page risks being a picture to tap unless the fault path is computed as a real circuit.

runnersUp.title: Fossils and rock layers
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: Superposition is core KS2/NGSS content and the burial-and-cut toy shows the mechanism; it is distinct from deep-time's dated timeline, though leadsTo radioactivity is a stretch.

build 3: Sediment deposition with porosity-depth compaction (Athy's law) and superposition is a real but very thin model, and the risk is a build-a-picture where layers stack because they are drawn; buildable only if burial depth, compaction and the cliff cut are computed, and the optional PBDB data (CC BY 4.0) is not needed.

runnersUp.title: Where your food goes
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A core primary curriculum topic with a staged mechanism (where each juice acts, absorption in the small intestine), distinct from homeostasis's blood-glucose view.

build 3: A compartment model with first-order breakdown and absorption is buildable, but the rates are rough textbook figures and the page leans toward a scripted scrub-through of a diagram; it needs the food-dependent emptying and breakdown to come from the model.

runnersUp.title: Taking a mixture apart
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A curriculum staple turned into a genuine build puzzle where each tool exploits one difference between particles, distinct from every existing page.

build 3: A rule-based particle sort through a chain of tools is honest at level 0 but closer to a puzzle state machine than a physical model. The chromatography strip could use real retention factors to give it substance.

runnersUp.title: Bubbles and foam
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: A real mechanism (surface tension pulling a film to least area) no existing page shows, with a pokeable film that is a great level-0 toy; arguably physics rather than chemistry.

build 3: A 2D closed film under tension and inside pressure relaxes to a circle, and two bubbles form a flat wall (Plateau), so those parts are buildable. Why plain water fails and soap holds (Marangoni stabilisation) and foam drainage are not captured honestly by a spring mesh, so narrow the page to the least-surface shape.

runnersUp.title: Autoencoders & variational autoencoders
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A navigable latent plane and the KL trade-off are a real mechanism distinct from diffusion's denoising, though it is a second generative-model page alongside diffusion-models.

build 4: Shipping a 2-D-latent AE and VAE trained offline on Fashion-MNIST (MIT) and running the decoders live is honest and small; the KL-weight slider needs a precomputed family of models (or a set of retrained checkpoints) since retraining on images live is too slow, which the entry should state.

runnersUp.title: How a phone counts your steps
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A threshold on a real accelerometer trace is an honest level-0 mechanism with a nice false-positive and false-negative trade-off, but it is thin and is signal processing more than AI.

build 4: Threshold and peak detection on real labelled HAPT accelerometer traces from UCI (CC BY 4.0, UCI's standard licence) is an honest, small model, and the entry is candid that there is no step ground truth and that the car trace is synthetic.

runnersUp.title: Normalizing flows
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Honest level 3 with a vivid change-of-variables graphic, but a niche generative family that fewer visitors will look for than VAEs or diffusion.

build 4: Affine coupling layers in 2-D have exact Jacobians and train on two-moons in seconds with hand-written gradients or a tiny autodiff; the density recoloring is an honest change-of-variables evaluation on a grid.

runnersUp.title: Why the app says 'you might also like'
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Co-visitation counts with a popularity pull and a cold-start problem form a real but thin mechanism, it sits close to pagerank's link-graph picture, and it repeats the batch's 'it's just counting' theme.

build 4: Item-to-item counts from a small CC0 Wikimedia Clickstream subset (licence confirmed) is an honest recommender, and following arrows is a real random walk that drifts toward hubs. It must keep the computation (drift, cold start) visible so it doesn't become a graph to browse.

runnersUp.title: How a speaker hears its name
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Building the spectrogram is a good visual, but the deciding step is a black-box network with confidence bars, so the page shows less mechanism than its level-0 siblings; it is still distinct from convolution-vision.

build 4: The TF.js speech-commands model (Apache 2.0, 18-word vocabulary) and Speech Commands clips (CC BY 4.0) run in the browser. The network itself is a black box, the shipped clips have to be pushed through the same WebAudio spectrogram pipeline the model expects, and the page adds a TF.js dependency.

runnersUp.title: Federated learning & differential privacy
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Federated averaging with client drift and a privacy-noise trade-off is a valid level-3 mechanism, but it is niche and bundles two topics (federation and differential privacy).

build 4: FedAvg over a few simulated clients with small 2-D models, plus clipping and Gaussian noise, is cheap and honest. The privacy budget slider must compute a real epsilon (for example from a moments accountant or a simple Gaussian-mechanism bound) rather than a label.

runnersUp.title: Distillation: a small model learning from a large one
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A real mechanism (soft targets at a temperature) with a clean comparison of loss curves, but it is less central to understanding LLMs than its siblings and partly repeats the training page's loss-curve race.

build 4: A shipped teacher (own weights) plus two small students training live on Tiny Shakespeare is feasible, and the soft-target bars are exact. The gap between the two loss curves must be measured on the real tiny models, since at this scale it may be small.

runnersUp.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: In high demand and its ranking is live, but the generation half is precomputed and the page is more a pipeline than one mechanism, which leans toward the embeddings and language-models pages.

build 4: BM25 and MiniLM embedding search over a few thousand CC BY-SA paragraphs run in the browser (Apache-2.0 model via transformers.js or precomputed vectors), and the answers with and without retrieval are honestly precomputed from an open small model for a fixed question set; the free-question path shows only retrieval, which should be stated.

runnersUp.title: World models & model-based RL
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The compounding error of imagined rollouts is a clear level-3 mechanism beyond grid-world RL, but it needs a live dynamics model plus a planner, which is heavy for its audience.

build 4: Cart-pole dynamics, a small MLP learning the next state online and Dyna- or MPC-style planning in imagination all run at interactive rates, and compounding model error is a real outcome of the learned model.

runnersUp.title: Dropout, weight decay & batch normalization
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Each technique is real, but bundling dropout, weight decay and batch norm reads as a survey of training tricks rather than one mechanism with one takeaway; it would be stronger narrowed to a single technique.

build 4: A small MLP on 2-D data trained live, TensorFlow-Playground style, with dropout, weight decay and batch norm is fully buildable. The many synchronised panels (boundary, histograms, per-layer activations) are a scope risk, not a buildability one.

runnersUp.title: Induction heads & in-context learning
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A real, testable circuit (shown by ablation) that is distinct from transformers, but it is research-frontier interpretability rather than what a typical university student learns, and it depends on precomputed training checkpoints.

build 4: A two-layer attention-only transformer with a tiny vocabulary is cheap to run forward and to ablate in the browser. The phase-change checkpoints must be trained offline (feasible on a laptop), with own weights and no external data.

runnersUp.title: Telescopes
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A good mechanism page (aperture and the diffraction limit) that is distinct from light-optics, but it is honestly level 2, the level the plan wants least, and it borders aperture-synthesis.

build 4: Ray tracing plus a computed Airy pattern on a synthetic star field, with seeing as a blur kernel, is all client-side and needs no data; it is broad (five sub-scenes) and should be scoped tightly.

runnersUp.title: Where your calories go
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The resting-versus-exercise energy budget is a useful counterintuitive takeaway and honest at level 0, but it is closer to an accounting display than a mechanism the graphic can show, and must avoid diet-advice framing.

build 4: Mifflin-St Jeor, Compendium MET values (numbers, free online) and USDA FoodData Central (public domain) give a real, openly sourced energy budget; buildable as an hourly stacked-block model, though it is closer to an explorable calculator than a simulation.

runnersUp.title: What an asteroid does when it hits
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The atmospheric-entry integration with fragmentation is a real model, but much of the page is published effect scalings drawn as rings, which leans toward a calculator; it is distinct from deep-time.

build 4: Integrating entry with drag, ablation and pancake breakup, then applying the published Collins-Melosh-Marcus scaling laws, is a small honest model; the equations come from a published paper, so no dataset licence is involved.

runnersUp.title: The Dirac equation
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: It is real and distinct, but a 1D Dirac spinor with Zitterbewegung and the Klein paradox is at the edge of graduate material, hard to make legible as a graphic, and appeals to fewer visitors than the core level-3 pages.

build 4: A 1D two-component Dirac packet solved by split-operator FFT is small and fast, and it shows Zitterbewegung and the Klein step honestly; it has to be done in momentum space to avoid fermion doubling on a naive grid.

runnersUp.title: Neutron stars & pulsars
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The P-Pdot diagram from ATNF data with dipole braking is real and distinct from stars, but it is mostly an explore of a catalogue, with a thinner mechanism than the other space candidates.

build 4: The P-Pdot diagram with dipole formulas and braking tracks is simple and honest; CSIRO's PSRCAT v2 record lists BSD 3-Clause with citation, so the data look reusable, though the catalogue's own site should confirm it.

runnersUp.title: Fluorescence, phosphorescence & photochemistry
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Competing decay routes on a Jablonski diagram are a valid kinetic model, but the graphic is mostly rate-constant bookkeeping with little to see, so its appeal is moderate.

build 4: First-order rate equations, or a stochastic population, for the competing decay routes give the lifetime, quantum yield, phosphorescent tail and Stern-Volmer line exactly; the model is small and honest, if close to a kinetics diagram, and the fluorophore lifetimes and yields are published facts.

runnersUp.title: Origin of life & the error threshold
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Eigen's error threshold is a real mechanism with a clear takeaway, but it is niche, overlaps population-genetics in machinery, and lists a level-3 candidate as a prerequisite.

build 4: A population of bit strings copied with errors on a single-peak landscape runs fast and shows the error threshold honestly; the replicase-evolution, parasite and compartment chapters add scope and should be kept lean.

runnersUp.title: Emoji and text as numbers
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An honest everyday entry point, but its core idea (a character is a number read by convention) is binary's takeaway at a simpler layer, so it is only partly distinct; the empty-box and SMS-counter details keep it worthwhile.

build 4: Encoding text to code points and to the GSM 7-bit or UCS-2 segment rules is real and small, and Unicode data is permissively licensed; the page must count an emoji as a surrogate pair (two UCS-2 units) so the counter is right.

runnersUp.title: Databases & queries
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Tables, keys, joins and indexes fill a real gap and the index row-count is a visible mechanism, but the page tries to cover normalisation, queries, indexes and transactions at once, and transactions overlap b-trees-transactions, so it should be trimmed to keys, joins and the index.

build 4: A tiny in-browser relational engine (filter, sort, hash/nested-loop join, index vs full scan with row counts) over Palmer penguins (CC0) or a GeoNames extract (CC BY 4.0) is real and fast; the concurrent-transaction scene needs to be a real interleaving, not a canned animation.

runnersUp.title: Maglev trains
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Eddy-current lift and drag against speed, and the unstable attractive design held by feedback, are real mechanisms, but they are two half-topics, and the second leans on feedback-control.

build 4: The analytic thin-sheet electrodynamic lift and drag formulas against speed, plus an unstable EMS ODE with a tunable controller, are small and honest. The drawn eddy-current pattern should come from the analytic solution, not be decoration.

runnersUp.title: Renormalization: the same picture at every scale
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Block-spin coarse-graining is a real and visual idea, but it is applied to the same Ising snapshots and could be a final step of ising-model rather than its own page.

build 4: Majority-rule 3x3 blocking of Ising snapshots is trivial, but critical snapshots on a 243- or 729-wide lattice need a Wolff cluster sampler or precomputed configurations, and the 'flow' plot is a correlation proxy, not a true coupling flow.

runnersUp.title: Satellites: the ones that race and the one that stays
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Ground tracks, the geostationary height and dusk visibility are appealing and distinct from orbits-kepler, but there are too many ideas and views for a one-control level-0 page; it should be trimmed to one takeaway.

build 4: Circular orbits over a rotating Earth give ground tracks, and a shadow-cylinder test gives visibility at dusk; this is honest geometry, ISS elements from NASA are public domain, and generic altitudes suffice for the other satellites.

runnersUp.title: The mole & reacting masses
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An honest, much-needed level-1 topic with a showable limiting-reagent mechanism, but it is closer to a calculation procedure than a 'how it works' phenomenon.

build 4: Balancing by atom counts, converting grams to moles with IUPAC atomic weights (openly available), and finding the limiting reagent are real algorithms, and the leftover reactant shows on screen; the risk is a worksheet rather than a scene, so the counts must be drawn as molecules.

runnersUp.title: Random walks & Brownian motion
judgeNotes: build 4: Thousands of walkers, root-mean-square growth, a histogram compared with the heat kernel and a self-similar path are easy; the return experiment can only show the fraction returned by time T, which saturates near 0.34 in 3D and creeps toward 1 slowly in 2D, so the page must not claim to show that every walker returns.

fit-level 3: The √t spreading and Pólya's recurrence across dimensions make a good level-3 page. It overlaps central-limit-theorem's Galton board and heat-and-wave-equations' diffusion, so it should lean on the recurrence and scale-invariance material.

runnersUp.title: Fixed points, Newton's method & its fractal
judgeNotes: build 4: Cobwebs and Newton tangents are trivial; the Newton basin image needs per-pixel iteration rendered to a raster image inside the SVG, which is affordable and has precedent in chaos-fractals' Mandelbrot zoom.

fit-level 3: Cobwebs, the role of the slope in convergence, and Newton basins make a sound mechanism at level 3. They sit close to chaos-fractals (cobwebbed logistic map, complex-plane fractal zoom) and partly to numerical-stability.

runnersUp.title: Fireworks: a bag of sparks thrown in every direction
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An appealing hook with a real mechanism (equal-speed stars form a sphere that falls together), but much of it is a sequence of stages and a colour table rather than one strong toy.

build 4: Ballistic shell plus hundreds of star particles with drag is a cheap, honest particle simulation. The metal-to-colour table is factual and easy to cite from an open reference, and NIST ASD is free US-government data with citation, though its licence page was not confirmed.

runnersUp.title: Pain & the gate in the spinal cord
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A small wired circuit that shows gating and sensitization is a real mechanism, but gate-control theory is a simplified, partly dated model and the page overlaps placebo-expectation's descending modulation.

build 4: A handful of integrate-and-fire neurons with wind-up via facilitation is a small, honest circuit simulation. Gate control is a simplified and partly contested theory, so the page must present it as a model circuit, not established anatomy.

runnersUp.title: Tor & onion routing
judgeNotes: build 4: Layered encryption as a stepped wrap and unwrap is near-diagrammatic, but the Monte Carlo of compromised circuits against the observer's fraction, plus timing correlation, gives it a real model.
fit-level 3: Layered encryption and the odds that an observer controls both ends make a clear, distinct mechanism, but the model is simple enough for a level-2 reader rather than university level.

runnersUp.title: Speed: how far each second
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Reading speed as the steepness of a distance-time line is honest at level 0 and is not the forces of newtons-laws, but it is a graph-reading lesson more than a mechanism and arguably belongs in physics.
build 4: Constant-speed runners with pauses plotted as distance against ticks is a trivial, honest kinematic model that animates as a pure function of time.

runnersUp.title: Markov chains
judgeNotes: build 4: Walkers on a small chain, the stationary eigenvector, absorption times and letter n-gram text generation are cheap; Eugene Onegin is public domain, but the page must recompute Markov's vowel–consonant counts from a named Wikisource edition rather than quote remembered numbers, and an order-3 English letter table should be built at build time to keep the bundle small.

fit-level 3: The general theory of stationary distributions, absorption and periodicity is a sound mechanism and a prerequisite for MCMC. Its core picture, walkers converging to a stationary distribution, repeats pagerank's random surfer, so the distinct value lies in the failure cases.

runnersUp.title: Where a bouncing ball's energy goes
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An honest level-0 toy, but the energy bars with a dissipated share already appear on newtons-laws, so the new part is mainly the choice of ball and floor.

build 4: Free fall plus a damped contact is honest and trivial. The per-ball and per-floor restitution values need a cited source rather than invented settings, and the thermometer must show the honestly tiny rise (mgh/mc, about hundredths of a degree).

runnersUp.title: Geothermal power
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The cold front breaking through between injector and producer is a real mechanism the graphic can show, and it is distinct from plate-tectonics, but the subject has limited demand and the binary cycle is an add-on.

build 4: An analytic doublet potential-flow field with a 2D advection-diffusion temperature grid over years runs at interactive rates. The cold-front breakthrough is directly visible, and only published rock properties are needed.

runnersUp.title: Bone remodelling
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Strain-driven remodelling that grows trabeculae (Wolff's law) is a real model with a striking emergent graphic, but a finite-element grid of thousands of elements is heavy to run as a pure function of time in the browser.

build 4: The Huiskes strain-adaptive rule on a 2D finite-element grid of a few thousand elements needs a linear solve per iteration, which a warm-started conjugate-gradient solver does in milliseconds, so trabeculae can emerge at interactive rates; it is iterative rather than a pure function of time, so iterations must be precomputed or cached for scrubbing.

runnersUp.title: Why toast goes brown
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The 'wet food is pinned at boiling, so it can't brown' mechanism is honest and level-0 friendly, but the browning model is thin and the page risks being one observation stretched across 6 to 9 steps.

build 4: A 1D heat-conduction model with an evaporating wet layer pinned at 100 °C plus an Arrhenius browning rate is small and honest, and a published Maillard activation energy is just a number; the page must not claim browning is zero below 100 °C, only far too slow to see.

runnersUp.title: Traffic lights that know you are there
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A queue simulation with a sensor rule is a legitimate mechanism from an everyday object, but its takeaway is thin and tuning green times to minimise total queue edges toward optimisation; its leadsTo targets (logic-gates, graph-search) are also loose.
build 4: A seeded random-arrival queue simulation with fixed-cycle and actuated controllers is a small honest discrete-event model, and the queue totals respond to the green split; no data needed.

runnersUp.title: Superconducting magnets & quench
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Its critical surface and quench propagation make a genuine, honestly level-3 mechanism distinct from fusion and imaging, but it is a niche specialist subject with less pull for visitors than the other candidates.

build 4: A 1D heat equation along the conductor with Joule heating switched on by a Bottura-fit critical surface, coupled to an L-R dump circuit, is a small explicit PDE plus ODE that runs fine in the browser; the fit parameters are published facts and the NIST cryogenic property fits are US-government public.

runnersUp.title: Synthetic gene circuits: toggle switch & repressilator
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The toggle switch and the repressilator are real level-3 synthetic biology, but the switch duplicates lac-operon/epigenetic bistability and the oscillator duplicates circadian-clocks within this file, so it is weaker unless it replaces one of them.

build 4: The repressilator (BioModels, CC0) and the Gardner toggle switch are small ODEs with a cheap stochastic version; the free-wiring builder needs a general ODE generator from the drawn graph, which can be built but is more UI work than the model.

runnersUp.title: The water cycle
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A sound level-1 page with residence times and Clausius-Clapeyron, but it largely repeats water-cycle (level 0) plus carbon-cycle's reservoir design, and its dew-point step duplicates dew-and-fog; build one of the two water pages.

build 4: A reservoir box model with residence time computed as stock divided by flux, a Markov walk for the tagged molecule and the Magnus formula is small and real; reservoir volumes are USGS public domain, but Oki and Kanae 2006 is not open, so take the fluxes from an open set (for example the USGS figure or Trenberth et al.) and keep it consistent.

runnersUp.title: Quantum scattering
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Partial-wave phase shifts and resonances are honest level 3 and distinct from the 1D barrier, but the appeal is narrower and the 3D wave is harder to make legible.
build 4: Partial-wave phase shifts for a spherical square well are closed-form spherical-Bessel expressions, so cross sections, resonances and a 2D slice of the scattered wave are cheap and honest.

runnersUp.title: Thermoelectric generators & coolers
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The 1D Seebeck/Peltier/Joule leg model and the ZT trade-off are a real level-3 mechanism, distinct from solar-cells, but the subject is niche and the graphic is mostly curves rather than a vivid moving mechanism.

build 4: The constant-property leg model (Seebeck, Peltier, Joule, conduction) is an honest closed form for efficiency, power and cooler limits versus current and ZT, and it checks out (about 0.2 of Carnot at ZT 1); temperature-dependent material curves are mostly in paywalled papers, so the page should use slider properties with typical Bi2Te3 values from open sources, and the graphic risks becoming mostly plots.

runnersUp.title: Flywheel energy storage
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The rotating-disc stress solution and the specific-strength argument form a clean level-3 model that no existing page covers, but it is a niche storage technology with modest visitor pull.

build 4: The analytic rotating-disc and rim stress solution, the energy, the burst speed from tabulated strength, and a coast-down ODE with friction and drag are all closed-form or tiny. Material strengths are published facts.

runnersUp.title: Going round a bend: steering and grip
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The sideways grip needed in a bend is a sound level-0 mechanism, but it shares the tyre-grip idea with the braking and friction candidates, and the Ackermann steering detail is marginal for a 10-year-old.
build 4: Ackermann geometry (both wheel axes meeting at one centre) and the required lateral force v²/r against μmg on a grip gauge are a small, honest kinematic model with no data needed.

runnersUp.title: Sugar syrup and caramel
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The thermometer-as-water-gauge insight is a real, distinct mechanism, but explaining a rising boiling point without formulas to a 10-year-old is delicate and the subject is niche.

build 4: Evaporation as an ODE plus the published curve of boiling point against sucrose concentration is a real, tiny model, and the thermometer genuinely reads the water left. Mapping the candy stages to concentration is an honest lookup, and the data is published facts.

runnersUp.title: Acid–base balance of blood
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The Davenport diagram with lungs and kidneys on two clocks is genuine level-3 physiology and distinct from acids-bases, but it is a narrow clinical tool and depends on two pool candidates (lung-gas-exchange, kidney-nephron) as prerequisites.

build 4: Henderson-Hasselbalch with a blood buffer line on a Davenport diagram, plus respiratory compensation in minutes and renal in days as first-order relaxations, is a real, cheap model whose trails are drawn by the model; the compensation rates need cited values.

runnersUp.title: Databases: B-trees & transactions
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: B+tree splits and write-ahead-log crash recovery are genuine level-3 database internals, but this is two topics in one page, and it depends on a pool candidate (locks-deadlock) and overlaps databases-and-queries on transactions.

build 4: A B+tree with adjustable fan-out and counted node reads, plus a write-ahead log with crash-and-replay and two isolation modes, are all small real algorithms; two models make it a large page but nothing needs a backend.

runnersUp.title: Transmission lines, AC and DC
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The long-line charging-current limit and the AC/DC break-even distance form a real level-3 model beyond power-grid's resistive loss, but the audience is narrow and phasors are hard to make visual.

build 4: The phasor long-line (telegrapher) equations with standard per-km constants compute voltage and current along the line instantly, and the charging-current limit and break-even distance emerge from them. Animating the phasors keeps it a function of time.

runnersUp.title: Angles are turns
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An honest level-0 bridge to unit-circle, and the total-turn walk is a real mechanism, but it sits close to a definition and shares its turn-closing idea with shapes-that-tile and sunflower-spirals in this same batch.
build 4: A turtle-geometry construction (heading accumulates exterior turns, summed on one pie) plus a divisibility check of steps-per-turn is a small, honest, level-0 model.

runnersUp.title: Plasma: shielding, oscillations & Landau damping
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A PIC plasma showing Debye shielding and Landau damping is real and distinct from nuclear-fusion, but it is specialist, and four sub-demos risk turning the page into a survey.
build 4: A 1D electrostatic particle-in-cell code is the honest model and runs in JS, but showing clean Landau damping needs tens of thousands of particles or a quiet start to beat the noise.

runnersUp.title: What soil is made of: the jar test
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A real home experiment with settling by grain size and drainage, but its sorting mechanism overlaps rock-to-sand, and the soil-naming part is closer to classification.

build 4: Settling by grain size and the USDA texture triangle (public domain) make an honest small model, but Stokes' law fails for sand, so use a settling law valid across sizes (for example Ferguson and Church 2004); infiltration should come from a simple texture-based conductivity, not drawn timings.

runnersUp.title: Heat from underground
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The gradient and the depleted-then-recovering well work at level 0, but the page leans toward a reading-and-map survey, and it would fit the energy category better than earth.

build 4: The geotherm from local heat flow and conductivity, plus a 1D radial conduction model of the ground cooling and recovering around a producing well, is small and honest; the IHFC Global Heat Flow Database 2024 release is CC BY 4.0 on GFZ Data Services (91k points, so ship a gridded subsample).

runnersUp.title: Supernova light curves
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The Arnett model with nickel-56 and cobalt decay is a real model with a good takeaway, but it is niche, and it shares the standard-candle thread with dark-energy-supernovae.

build 4: The Arnett model with Ni-to-Co-to-Fe heating is a one-integral semi-analytic model that is cheap and honest; one observed light curve is needed, and the Pantheon+ licence is unconfirmed, so a CC BY or public source should be found.

runnersUp.title: Keeping a chip cool
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Thermal resistances in series and hotspot concentration form a real mechanism, distinct from cpu, but the core idea is close to level 2 and overlaps the conduction part of heat-transfer-insulation.

build 4: A 2D/3D heat-diffusion grid on a die with a series resistance stack, plus a throttling loop, runs easily in the browser. The hotspot-versus-area effect emerges from the model, and conductivities are published facts.

runnersUp.title: Mirrors & turns: symmetry
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An honest level-0 drawing toy, but it leans toward a definition with counting, its mechanism is thin, and its link to unit-circle is weak.
build 4: Live reflection and n-fold rotation of a drawn path, and testing a polygon or glyph outline against each flip and turn for coincidence, is a clean geometric construction with no data.

runnersUp.title: Radiocarbon calibration
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Mapping a radiocarbon age through IntCal20 plateaus and wiggle-matching is a real and distinct step beyond radioactivity, but it is narrow and sits in the same dating family as isotope-dating-concordia.

build 4: Calibration is a likelihood over a curve of a few thousand points and wiggle-matching is a 1D offset search, both trivial; the IntCal20 curve comes with the CC BY 4.0 Radiocarbon paper and is free from intcal.org, so ship it from the paper's supplement with credit rather than through the GPL R package (confirm the intcal.org terms).

runnersUp.title: Perturbation theory
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An honest level-3 method with a good exact-against-series comparison, but it is a technique rather than a phenomenon, so fewer visitors will want it, and it leans on two other pool pages (hydrogen-atom, quantum-harmonic-oscillator).

build 4: Diagonalising the anharmonic oscillator in a truncated basis and running a basis TDSE for golden-rule transitions are small, honest computations; the hydrogen Stark case is harder because the exact states are resonances, so it should become a box or oscillator in a field.

runnersUp.title: Inflation & the horizon problem
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The comoving Hubble radius plot is the right level-3 tool, but the graphic is abstract and the subject is a hypothesis, so it is less of a must-have than the CMB or the cosmic web.

build 4: The Friedmann equations plus a slow-roll scalar-field ODE, with the comoving Hubble radius plotted on log axes, are a small honest model; the reader-shaped potential needs guarding so it still yields about 60 e-folds.

runnersUp.title: The critical point & supercritical fluids
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The equal-area construction and critical point are honest level-3 thermodynamics, but states-of-matter already tracks a phase diagram so the new part is the end of the liquid-gas line, a narrower gain.

build 4: The vdW isotherms, Maxwell equal-area construction and coexistence dome are an exact, tiny computation using NIST critical constants. The weak part is the particle box: near-critical 2D molecular dynamics is slow and noisy, so it should be clearly qualitative or reuse the states-of-matter engine.

runnersUp.title: Why batteries wear out
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: High everyday demand, but the model is a fitted semi-empirical curve rather than a mechanism the graphic can show working, and it sits close to lithium-cell-dynamics in the same batch; one of the two battery pages may be enough.

build 4: Evaluating a semi-empirical calendar-plus-cycle ageing law over a usage pattern is cheap and honest, though the 'knee' is not produced by the Schmalstieg law and needs a separate published mechanism. The NASA PCoE ageing data's licence is unconfirmed (data.gov lists no licence for the Li-ion ageing set), so confirm it or use an openly licensed dataset for the overlay.

runnersUp.title: Where the socket's electricity comes from
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A real-data scrub of the generation mix is engaging but closer to a data tour than a mechanism, and it partly overlaps power-grid and power-station-kettle.

build 4: A scrubbable year of EIA-930 hourly generation by fuel (US government, public domain; about 8,760 rows times a few fuels) is a small shipped dataset that honestly shows the daily and seasonal shares; the wire-following path from lamp to plant is decoration around that data.

runnersUp.title: Metabolic networks & flux balance
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: An honest level-3 systems-biology model (FBA by linear programming) with visible flux rerouting, but it is niche for this site's visitors and heavy to build in the browser.

build 4: Flux balance analysis on a core network of around 100 reactions is a small LP that a JS simplex solves in milliseconds, but the network must be built from textbook stoichiometry with citations because BiGG e_coli_core is not openly licensed.

runnersUp.title: Turbulence: the energy cascade
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A genuine level-3 subject with a real (shell) model, but the graphic is mostly a log-log spectrum rather than visible eddies, and it depends on a navier-stokes page that does not yet exist.

build 4: A GOY or Sabra shell model has about 20 complex ODEs, runs easily in the browser and reproduces the -5/3 spectrum, so it is the honest reduced model at level 3. The spectrum needs time-averaging and a stiff-aware integrator, and the page must say it is a shell model, not Navier-Stokes.

runnersUp.title: A battery is a bucket of pushes
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A good level-0 everyday question (brighter lamp means shorter life), but the series/parallel content leans on electric-circuits, and the 'bucket of pushes' metaphor misstates what a battery stores, so the framing needs fixing.

build 4: A capacity-and-discharge model of an AA cell driving a resistive bulb in series and parallel is small and honest, with the capacity and curve shape quoted as facts from a datasheet; the bulb's changing resistance can be simplified at level 0 without misleading.

runnersUp.title: Seismic tomography
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A regularized inversion with uneven ray coverage and checkerboard resolution tests is a real level-3 method, but its core idea (an image computed from many path measurements) partly repeats medical-imaging and earthquakes.

build 4: Ray tracing through a radially layered PREM (the published table values are facts) plus a damped LSQR inversion over a few hundred cells and rays is small and honest, and the checkerboard test is exactly what the real method does.

runnersUp.title: A year of weather, two places
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The weather-versus-climate distinction is a valuable level-0 idea built on real data, but the page shows a pattern rather than a mechanism and is closer to a data explorer than a how-it-works page.

build 4: A small shipped dataset (five US GHCN-Daily stations over a few years, public domain) drawn as rings is honest and light. It is a data-scrub page rather than a model, which is acceptable at level 0 (like deep-time).

runnersUp.title: Symmetry & groups
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Composing symmetries into a Cayley table is a genuine level-3 mechanism, but the page splits across two large subjects (finite groups and the 17 wallpaper groups), and the wallpaper part risks turning into a catalogue.

build 4: Composing dihedral elements into a Cayley table and tiling a motif with wallpaper-group generators are exact constructions, but cycling all 17 groups is a lot of hand-built geometry, and the 'counter' for why 5-fold rotation never closes is undefined (better as the crystallographic restriction shown on a lattice).

runnersUp.title: Flowers and bees
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Pollination as a trade counted in seeds is level-0 honest and distinct from predator-prey, but the model is thin and the outcome (no bees, fewer seeds) is predictable.

build 4: Foraging agents attracted by colour, with pollen carryover and dilution and seed set requiring conspecific pollen, form an honest small agent simulation with countable outcomes. It needs no external data, though the attraction and carryover parameters are illustrative and should be described as such.

runnersUp.title: Roller coasters: where the heavy and floaty moments come from
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Felt weight in dips and loops plus the first-hill rule is engaging, but newtons-laws already has an editable track with energy, so its distinct part is mainly the felt-weight gauge.

build 4: A bead on a reader-drawn spline with friction and normal force computed from curvature is a standard real-time model and an honest source for felt weight and leaving the track; it overlaps heavily with the newtons-laws track, which is a duplication concern rather than a buildability one.

runnersUp.title: Why an e-reader looks like paper
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Charged specks that stay put once moved are a neat, honest level-0 mechanism, but the device is niche and the page has fewer steps of real substance than the stronger candidates.

build 4: Oppositely charged particles drifting at Stokes speed in a capsule under a switchable field are a small honest particle model that shows bistability. Reflected versus emitted light under room dimming is a simple toggle, and the page should say whether it draws the two-pigment or the dyed-oil design.

runnersUp.title: Tuning a radio
judgeNotes: build 4: A sum of carriers through a resonant band-pass filter followed by envelope and FM detection is an honest small DSP model; scaled-down carrier frequencies plus Web Audio output are needed and should be stated.

fit-level 3: Choosing a station by resonance is a sound mechanism and new in its many-stations framing, but it leans on oscillations-resonance, and the AM/FM comparison risks overloading a level-0 page that should offer one control at a time.

runnersUp.title: Magnetohydrodynamics: frozen-in field lines
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Honest level-3 MHD with a visible mechanism (field lines wound up by the flow), distinct from nuclear-fusion, but niche, and it depends on navier-stokes from the pool.

build 4: The kinematic induction equation for a vector potential, advected by a prescribed 2D flow with magnetic diffusion, is a small grid PDE and shows freezing-in honestly; the plucked Alfvén wave needs the field to push back on the fluid, so it should be a separate 1D model.

runnersUp.title: Conic sections & projective geometry
judgeNotes: build 4: Cone sections, a perspective camera on a floor circle, the cross-ratio and Pascal's line are exact constructions; the cone-and-plane view needs careful 3D-to-SVG projection, but this is still geometry, not a picture to tap.

fit-level 3: The page glues two subjects: conic sections, which are level 1 or 2, and projective invariants such as cross-ratio and Pascal's theorem, which are level 3. That split weakens its focus, though it is distinct from graphics-3d.

runnersUp.title: Generating functions
judgeNotes: build 4: Multiplying polynomials for coins and dice and expanding a rational function's series are exact and cheap; collapsing the Fibonacci series to a fraction is a known closed form shown rather than general symbolic algebra, which is fine for the page.

fit-level 3: Multiplying polynomials to count coin and dice combinations is a real mechanism, and the level is honest. The subject is closer to formal bookkeeping than a visible process, and its appeal is narrower.

runnersUp.title: Wound healing
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A travelling-wave reaction-diffusion model is a genuine level-3 mechanism, but the infection and diabetes effects are only stated rate cuts, and the subject draws weaker demand than the other medicine candidates.

build 4: The Sherratt–Murray two-variable reaction–diffusion on a 2D grid with a user-drawn wound runs easily and gives a travelling-wave closure. Infection and diabetes are honestly stated as parameter cuts, and the healing stages are labels only.

runnersUp.title: The infinite hotel
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Pairing rooms with guests is a real idea a curious 10-year-old can follow and no existing page touches infinity, but it is a thought experiment rather than a mechanism, and it leads to no existing topic.
build 4: Applying a room-reassignment function to a lazily rendered, scrollable row and enumerating rationals by a diagonal walk is a real algorithm that runs instantly in the browser.

runnersUp.title: Convexity, Lagrange multipliers & duality
judgeNotes: build 4: For a 2D objective with one constraint, the gradients, Lagrange point, a dual function computed by inner minimisation over a grid, and the shadow price are all cheap to compute; the non-convex toggle needs carefully chosen example functions so the duality gap shows clearly.

fit-level 3: Gradient alignment at a constrained optimum and the multiplier as a price are real level-3 content, and the page adds constraints to gradient-descent. The dual-function panel is abstract for a general visitor, and the shadow price overlaps linear-programming.

runnersUp.title: Kites: how a string holds you to the wind
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Balancing the wind's push, weight and string tension on a kite is a showable level-0 mechanism, but it overlaps the other wing-family candidates (paper plane, sailing, helicopter) and partly the flight page.

build 4: A 2D flat-plate kite with a bridle point, weight, tail drag and string tension can be integrated or solved for equilibrium in real time, and cutting the line is the same ODE with tension zero; the flat-plate lift and drag curves should be stated as a simplification.

runnersUp.title: The Casimir effect
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A real level-3 mode-sum model, but it is niche, the cutoff-independence is abstract to show, and it reuses the cavity-mode machinery of blackbody-cavity-modes in this same file, so it would work better as a step there.

build 4: A 1D mode sum with a smooth cutoff in a three-plate (piston) geometry gives a cutoff-independent finite force and runs instantly. The page must state that 1D gives a 1/a^2 force while real 3D plates give 1/a^4.

runnersUp.title: The field of a moving charge
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The retarded-field kink is a beautiful and correct mechanism, distinct from static electromagnetism, but it overlaps considerably with maxwell-equations (a source on the Yee grid also radiates), so one of the two should probably host the other.

build 4: Field lines built from the stored trajectory and retarded times (the known Liénard-Wiechert kink construction) run interactively and show the radiation kink and the relativistic pancake directly.

runnersUp.title: Estimating: count a little, multiply
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Count a patch and multiply is a usable method that fits level 0 and lets the reader pick a bad patch, but it is thin as a mechanism and the graphic has little to show beyond one multiplication.

build 4: A generated non-uniform point field (a 2D settling pile or a density-mapped crowd) with a window count, scale-up and true total is an honest sampling model; the 'real pile' should be a simple deposition or density field, not a photo, and needs no data.

runnersUp.title: Pushing a swing
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A good level-0 entry to oscillations-resonance, but its takeaways (length sets the period; well-timed pushes build up) are largely that page's own pendulum and resonance, simplified.

build 4: The pendulum ODE with timed impulses, plus pumping as a time-varying effective length or centre-of-mass shift, is buildable and honest, though the seated-pumping model must be chosen carefully (it is driven, not simply parametric).

runnersUp.title: Speciation
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Dobzhansky-Muller incompatibilities snowballing is a genuine mechanism, but it builds on population-genetics, a level-3 candidate, and its graphic is more abstract than its siblings'.

build 4: An explicit two-population, multi-locus simulation with random pairwise Dobzhansky-Muller incompatibilities is cheap and makes the snowball emerge rather than be drawn; migration and reinforcement are extra parameters on the same model.

runnersUp.title: Why bruises change colour
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Haemoglobin breakdown through green and yellow is a real sequence a child has seen on their own skin, but the toy is mostly a colour timeline with one control, and it sits near how-cuts-heal in theme.

build 4: First-order conversion haemoglobin to biliverdin to bilirubin with clearance, in a spreading pool, colour mixed from the three pigments' absorption, is a small honest kinetic model; the rate constants must be given as ranges, as the entry says.

runnersUp.title: Rectangles & primes
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Finding primes by trying rectangles is a nice level-0 way in, but its takeaway (which counts are prime and where they fall) largely repeats what primes-modular-arithmetic's sieve already shows.
build 4: Enumerating factor pairs to lay out chairs and lighting single-line counts on a hundred-square is a small exact algorithm that draws directly.

runnersUp.title: The segmentation clock
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The clock-and-wavefront model is a distinct, elegant mechanism, but it is a third pattern-formation page beside morphogen-gradients and turing-patterns and leans on a level-3 prerequisite.
build 4: A strip of Lewis delay-differential oscillators with Notch coupling and a moving wavefront is a small DDE system that runs interactively with a history buffer; no data needed.

runnersUp.title: Helicopters: a spinning wing
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The rotating wing, disc tilt and tail-rotor torque reaction are a genuine level-0 mechanism, but this is one of four wing-family candidates in the batch (with kite, paper plane and sailing), so it competes with them for a place.

build 4: Momentum-theory thrust from spin and collective, a tilted thrust vector and a yaw ODE for torque reaction make a small rigid-body sim that is honest at level 0, though blade-element detail must stay out.

runnersUp.title: Version control & Merkle trees
judgeNotes: build 4: Content hashing (SHA-1 or SHA-256 via SubtleCrypto), an object DAG, a Myers diff with three-way merge and Merkle proofs are all real and small, though the scope is broad.

fit-level 3: Content addressing, three-way merge and Merkle proofs are a real mechanism, but the hash-chain tamper demo partly repeats consensus-blockchains, and the page mixes two subjects (git and Merkle proofs).

runnersUp.title: Nuclear reaction networks in stars

build 4: A roughly 15-species stiff network with Caughlan-Fowler analytic rates (published formulas) integrates quickly with an implicit solver; REACLIB has no confirmed licence, so use CF88.

runnersUp.title: Why a shot protects you
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A head-start race of counts is an honest level-0 framing, but its takeaway (memory is already in place) is the same as mrna-vaccines and immune-system's second response, so it is a simpler retelling rather than a new mechanism.

build 4: Exponential pathogen growth racing a clonal expansion that starts from a handful versus thousands of memory cells is a tiny ODE with textbook timescales, and the head start is visible in the curves; honest at level 0.

runnersUp.title: Dams and water wheels: the push is in the height
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Height times flow as a comparison works at level 0 and is distinct from power-grid, but the mechanism is thin (one product of two quantities) and the waterfall and reservoir parts dilute it.

build 4: Torricelli outflow, power proportional to flow times head and a draining reservoir are a small honest model, and the equal-power comparison of high head against high flow comes straight out of it.

runnersUp.title: Car brakes
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Familiar and mechanistic, but it packs three ideas (lever, hydraulic multiplication, speed-squared stopping distance) into one level-0 page with one control at a time; it should be trimmed to the hydraulic chain or to stopping distance.

build 4: A lever, Pascal's-law hydraulic ratio, pad friction and v-squared stopping distance with a friction limit for skidding make a small honest chain of models, though it is two pages' worth of content and should be kept tight.

runnersUp.title: Colloids: why particles stay apart, and when they stick
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: DLVO stability and salt-induced flocculation are a genuine level-3 model with a nice real-world hook (river deltas), but niche, and it depends on the proposed dispersion-forces page.

build 4: Brownian dynamics of a few hundred particles under the DLVO pair potential (van der Waals plus screened double-layer repulsion with a Debye length set by salt and valence) runs easily in the browser, and flocculation and the strong valence dependence emerge from it; no data is needed.

runnersUp.title: Escalator
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A neat geometric mechanism (rigid steps kept level by two offset tracks), but it is narrow, and leadsTo unit-circle is a stretch.

build 4: A real geometric construction (a rigid step on two wheel pairs riding two offset tracks) stays level, or tilts when the reader moves the tracks; the comb-and-groove zoom is the only part that is just a picture.

runnersUp.title: Metal detectors
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Eddy-current echoes are a real mechanism and an appealing device, but induction stretches what a 10-year-old can grasp without field ideas, and it should lead to electromagnetism more than to electric-circuits.

build 4: A search coil coupled to a target as a small RL loop, with mutual inductance falling off steeply with depth, is a small honest model that distinguishes conductors from a stone and shows the depth-versus-coil-size trade-off.

runnersUp.title: Feynman diagrams
judgeNotes: fit-level 4: High demand, and turning diagrams into a tree-level calculator checked against LEP data is a real mechanism well beyond standard-model's beta-decay step-through; it does lean on perturbation-theory, which is also in the pool.

build 2: No browser can evaluate amplitudes from an arbitrary drawn diagram, so the 'calculator' would be a lookup of a few closed-form cross sections; also, at 192-208 GeV LEP data are dominated by Z exchange, so pure QED would not match. HEPData is CC0, but record 48691 is the muon A_FB table, so the cross-section companion tables are also needed. Keep only if narrowed to a fixed set of processes with γ+Z formulas.

runnersUp.title: Smell and taste

build 2: The receptor 'locks' are an invented toy matrix unless an open odorant-receptor response dataset (for example Pyrfume-hosted data, licence to be checked per set) fills it, and the pinched-nose strawberry is a picture to tap; the combinatorial-code idea survives only if the matrix comes from real data.

runnersUp.title: Why a photo cannot unlock your phone

build 3: Ray-casting a dot pattern onto a parametric head and comparing depth maps is a real triangulation model and works without data. The match score and the twin case are toy stand-ins for a real face-ID network, though, so the page has to say the matcher is simplified.

runnersUp.title: Contrastive & self-supervised learning

build 3: An InfoNCE encoder on a Fashion-MNIST subset (MIT) is feasible as precomputed checkpoints, but live training with augmentations is slow in the browser. The CLIP variant has no real text data behind it, so it would be a toy, and it should be cut or narrowed to label-name text.

runnersUp.title: Rust
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Water plus air plus salt is a familiar KS3 experiment, but the model is an empirical rate grid with no visible mechanism of why iron and oxygen combine, so the toy explains less than it shows.

build 3: A grid automaton with wetness- and salt-dependent rates is buildable, but the relative rates are loosely sourced and the electrochemical mechanism is hidden. Anchor the rates to published corrosivity categories (ISO 9223) rather than invented numbers.

runnersUp.title: Water pressure & hydraulics
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Pressure growing with depth and hydraulic force multiplication are honest level-0 ideas, but the page bundles two mechanisms and its hydraulic lift repeats the same step in fluid-pressure-buoyancy in this file.

build 3: Hydrostatics, Torricelli and Pascal are trivially buildable. However, the honest Torricelli model contradicts the interaction: jets landing at the bottle's base level reach furthest from the middle hole (range 2*sqrt(h(H-h))), not the lowest, so the bottle must stand on a raised support or the claim must change.

runnersUp.title: Friction, bearings & lubrication
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The page solves the Reynolds-equation pressure wedge and sweeps the Stribeck curve, a genuine mechanism that replaces newtons-laws' friction coefficient and fits an engineering level 3, but its everyday hook (oil) is undersold and its appeal is moderate.

build 3: The 1D Reynolds equation, or the Sommerfeld solution, gives an honest film pressure and hydrodynamic friction, but the boundary and mixed parts of the Stribeck curve are not in that model and would need an empirical asperity-contact blend (e.g. Greenwood-Williamson), and ISO 3448 itself is a paywalled standard, though grade viscosities and the Walther fit are widely published.

runnersUp.title: Allergy, IgE & anaphylaxis
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The bell-shaped crosslinking curve is a real but narrow mechanism; it shares its circulation-collapse ending with sepsis-inflammation, so one of the two is enough.

build 3: The bivalent-crosslinking equilibrium (Dembo–Goldstein) is honest and gives the bell curve. The histamine-to-blood-pressure circulation and desensitization are glued-on toy compartments with no sourced parameters, so half the page would be a dressed-up picture.

runnersUp.title: How a cut heals
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Platelet plug and scab under new skin is a real mechanism from an everyday experience and works at level 0, though the cut-depth and scab-picking controls make a thinner toy than its sibling healing candidates.

build 3: Platelet particles sticking at a leak until the flow stops is an honest, cheap simulation; the scab and the creeping skin cells are a second, mostly scripted grid, and 'pick the scab and it reopens' is a rule rather than a model, so the page is half model and half animation.

runnersUp.title: Where the work goes: exergy

runnersUp.title: What a remote control says

fit-level 3: A charming level-0 object with a real protocol (NEC-style pulse gaps) and a phone-camera hook, but the mechanism is thin and overlaps the barcode and binary ideas.

runnersUp.title: Inside an egg

runnersUp.title: Hydroelectric turbines

runnersUp.title: Substitution mechanisms: SN1 and SN2

runnersUp.title: Sailing against the wind

runnersUp.title: Scaling a recipe

runnersUp.title: Fractions: fair shares

runnersUp.title: The cosmic distance ladder
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The error propagation up the rungs is a good mechanism, but parallax, Cepheid calibration and the Hubble law are first-year material rather than level 3, and the page partly overlaps dark-energy-supernovae.

build 3: Propagating errors up the ladder is a simple, honest computation, but every rung's data has an unconfirmed licence (Gaia is free with credit, OGLE and SH0ES are unclear), so the dataset must be checked or cut to small retyped tables with citations before building.

runnersUp.title: What a smoke alarm senses
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Both sensing mechanisms are real and showable, but ionisation-chamber current capture is a stretch for a 10-year-old, and the page reads more like a device tour than one takeaway toy.

build 3: Ion drift and capture by smoke particles and light scattering onto a sensor can be an agent sim, but the flaming-versus-smouldering response difference depends on particle size distributions that a level-0 toy model would have to assume, so there is a risk of a picture with dots unless the size dependence of capture and scattering is actually modelled.

runnersUp.title: Treasure maps: coordinates & scale
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Honest level 0 and distinct from graph-search, but naming a spot with two numbers and reading a scale bar is mostly a definition, with little mechanism for the graphic to show.
build 3: Ordered-pair placement and polyline length times a scale factor are honest but thin computations; buildable, with the scale-invariance step the only real model behaviour.

runnersUp.title: Why you feel full
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Stomach stretch and gastric emptying rates give a genuine, formula-free mechanism with a nice same-energy comparison, distinct from homeostasis's blood-sugar loop, though the satiety story is simplified (hormones are left out) and the page must not overclaim.

build 3: Gastric emptying by food type is a small compartment model with published half-times, but the fullness gauge is an invented function of volume plus a gut signal, and the soup-versus-snack takeaway rests entirely on that invented weighting; it needs a cited satiety relation to count as a model.

runnersUp.title: Sea-level fingerprints
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The sea-level equation's surprising gravitational fingerprint is a real level-3 mechanism and sea level is missing from the catalogue, but the page has a single idea and a narrower audience.

build 3: The rigid-Earth sea-level equation is linear in melt, so the fingerprint of each source can be computed offline (spherical-harmonic or Green's-function convolution with an ocean-function iteration) and only scaled in the page; that is honest but the live part is thin. ETOPO is NOAA public domain, while the ice-sheet masks need a named openly licensed source (e.g. BedMachine/IMBIE) that is not yet given.

runnersUp.title: Your pulse
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Counting your own pulse is a lovely hands-on start, but the mechanism is thin and partly covered by heart-circulation's rate control, so it would be stronger folded into a level-0 heart page.

build 3: Heart rate following effort with exponential recovery and a pulse-wave delay is a real but very thin model, and the pulse-counting stopwatch is a tool rather than a model; it risks reading as an animation with sliders.

runnersUp.title: Where sand comes from
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A good level-0 story, but its size sorting where the river slows repeats river-valleys' deposition and soil-in-a-jar's settling, so it would be better merged with one of them.

build 3: Sternberg's abrasion law and settling speeds by grain size are real but give one exponential and one sort, so as a step-through story it risks being a picture sequence; buildable if the grain sizes along the river are computed from those laws for the chosen rock type.

runnersUp.title: Self-tolerance & autoimmunity
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The two-threshold selection trade-off is a clean mechanism distinct from immune-system's clonal expansion, but the model is thin and close to a single plotted histogram.

build 3: Buildable honestly only if affinity comes from a sequence model, such as the Košmrlj–Chakraborty string-matching model of TCR and peptide. Drawn as independent random numbers, the challenge step becomes circular and the page a toy.

runnersUp.title: Why big birds flap slowly
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: A good everyday question, but the mechanism is a scaling law that a level-0 page must state as 'the sums stop working' rather than show, so it risks being a correlation chart; it is distinct from flight's wing section.

build 3: Pennycuick's scaling formula and the minimum speed from wing loading make a small honest model, but AVONET has mass and wing length and neither wingspan nor wing area, which the formula needs, and the Figshare record shows no clear licence; ship a small table of species with measured span, area and wingbeat frequency (Pennycuick's published tables, or Alerstam et al. 2007, PLoS Biology, CC BY) instead.

runnersUp.title: The liver & drug interactions
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: Extraction ratio and first-pass metabolism are a real mechanism but a narrow extension of pharmacokinetics-dosing in this batch, and it would work better as a section of that page.

build 4: The well-stirred hepatic model and Michaelis–Menten alcohol elimination are closed-form and honest, but the example high- and low-extraction drugs need sourced parameters (e.g. FDA labels, public domain), which the entry does not name.

runnersUp.title: Lighthouses: how far a light can be seen
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: Only the horizon geometry is a mechanism; flash rhythms are a list of conventions, so the page reads more as trivia than how-it-works and sits oddly in earth.

build 4: Geographic range from lamp and eye heights over a curved Earth, plus flash characteristics from the USCG Light List (US-government XML, freely downloadable), is a small honest geometric model; it is thin, so the ship's sighting must be computed from the horizon geometry and not scripted.

runnersUp.title: Choosing a material: composites & Ashby charts
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: The Ashby chart is mostly a selection survey with little mechanism; the rule of mixtures and fibre pull-out give it some substance, but it is weaker than the other materials candidates.

build 2: The only real model is the rule of mixtures plus a selection-line ranking; the rest is panning a property chart, close to browsing a diagram, and the data is weak: Materials Project (CC BY 4.0) gives only computed moduli of crystals, so polymers, woods and composites need a hand-compiled table, and the fibre pull-out panel would be a picture.

runnersUp.title: Caterpillar to butterfly
judgeNotes: fit-level 3: Appealing and honest for level 0, but it is mostly a staged life-cycle sequence of facts with a weak model (moulting because skin cannot stretch), so less of a toy than its peers.

build 2: Degree-day development (Zalucki 1982 thresholds, facts) and an instar mass curve are real but tiny models. The core of the page is stepping through life-stage drawings and a cutaway of the pupa, which is close to a browse-a-diagram with a temperature multiplier.

runnersUp.title: The placebo effect
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: The Bayesian cue-combination model is normative rather than a mechanism, and its trial-arm half (regression to the mean, natural recovery) duplicates clinical-trials in this batch.

build 3: The Bayesian core is just a precision-weighted mean of two Gaussians, which is thin as an interactive model. The three-arm trial with regression to the mean adds a real simulation, but the conditioning-over-trials part needs a stated learning rule.

runnersUp.title: Ice skates: glide forward, grip sideways
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: Glide along the blade and grip across it is a nice idea, but why ice is slippery is still debated by scientists, so the zoom on a 'thin wet layer' risks teaching something uncertain as fact, and the page mixes a friction survey with blade mechanics.

build 3: The sled comparison is a trivial friction ODE and the blade is an anisotropic-friction rigid body, both buildable, but ice friction coefficients depend on speed and temperature (one cited table must be chosen and named), and the wet-layer zoom is a picture, not a model.

runnersUp.title: Umbrella
judgeNotes: fit-level 2: A simple linkage plus flipping inside out is thin as a 'how it works' subject and weakly linked to anything the site teaches next.

build 3: The runner, stretcher and rib linkage is honest planar kinematics, but turning inside out is snap-through buckling, which a level-0 model can only approximate with a threshold on rib bending, so that part is close to a picture.
